extracted.intended_audience: banks, credit unions, AML/CFT compliance officers, legal/regulatory counsel, and other stakeholders submitting comments to the Agencies
extracted.subtask_description: A notice-and-comment supplemental information document soliciting stakeholder input on a proposed inter-Agency AML/CFT program rule, addressing program elements, risk-assessment processes, governance, testing, supervision, disclosure, economic impacts, and implementation timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of an “Effective” AML/CFT Program
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule sets forth the conditions for an effective AML/CFT program. Is the description of an effective program sufficiently clear or is there anything further that the Agencies should consider in the final rule adding to clarify program effectiveness?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Agencies welcome comment on whether the description is sufficiently clear and what additional language or examples would clarify program effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Banks’ Discretion to Identify Risks and Allocate Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule reflects a determination by the Agencies that banks are best placed to identify risks and allocate resources, and that providing them with greater discretion in these areas will improve the quality of AML/CFT compliance and reporting to law enforcement. Is this correct or should the Agencies consider adding more requirements regarding allocation of resources?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters should address whether banks should have that discretion, whether more prescriptive allocation requirements are needed, and how banks might assess changes in total allocation of resources devoted to AML/CFT in a changing risk and cost environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction Between Establishing and Maintaining an AML/CFT Program
rubrics_metrics.description: Do banks distinguish between establishing a program and maintaining a program by implementing the program? If so, how? Should the Agencies add anything to further define these terms in the final rule?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicits input on whether the proposed distinction is meaningful to banks and whether regulatory text should define or refine these terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whether Distinction Should Be Modified or Is Useful
rubrics_metrics.description: Should the proposed rule's distinction between “establishing” and “maintaining” a program be modified? Is the distinction between “establishing” and “maintaining” a compliance program useful for banks?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asks whether the binary is helpful or should be altered to better reflect practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing vs Maintaining at Program Level vs Element Level
rubrics_metrics.description: Should the proposed rule distinguish between “establishing” and “maintaining” at the program level and “establishing” and “maintaining” each individual element? For example, should the final rule more clearly differentiate between a failure to establish the program, as a whole, versus a failure to establish an individual mandatory component of the program?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seeks comment on whether failures should be characterized differently depending on whether they affect the whole program or individual mandatory components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification of “Significant or Systemic Failure” to Implement
rubrics_metrics.description: Is clarification needed for banks to determine what constitutes a “significant or systemic failure” to implement in all material respects a properly established AML/CFT program?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asks whether additional definitions or examples are needed so banks and supervisors can determine what is significant or systemic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification of “Failure to Establish an AML/CFT Program”
rubrics_metrics.description: Is clarification needed for banks to determine what constitutes a “failure to establish an AML/CFT program”?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests input on whether the rule should further define or provide examples of what constitutes a failure to establish a program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of Rulemaking Authority Between FinCEN and the Agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: How should the proposed rule ensure that the regulations issued by FinCEN and the appropriate Agencies function harmoniously? How should the proposed rule differentiate between the Secretary of the Treasury's responsibility for regulations on establishing AML/CFT programs and the Agencies' responsibilities for regulations on establishing and maintaining programs?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicits comments about coordination, role delineation, and harmonization between FinCEN and the banking Agencies to avoid conflicting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal Policies, Procedures, and Controls Must Be Risk-Based and Reasonably Designed
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule requires that internal policies, procedures, and controls be “risk-based” and “reasonably designed” to ensure compliance with the BSA. Do banks expect any changes to their existing internal policies, procedures, and controls under the proposed rule?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asks whether these standards are clear, how they would change current practice, and what implementation impacts might be expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Multiple Risk Assessment Processes
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule refers to risk assessment processes rather than a risk assessment process. This leaves banks free to use findings from one or more processes to assess their ML/TF risk. Does this description of how banks assess their ML/TF risk provide sufficient flexibility? How should the Agencies describe “risk assessment processes” to better reflect how banks assess ML/TF risks?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seeks views on whether pluralizing 'process' is appropriate and how to describe acceptable approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional or Different Criteria to Include in Risk Assessment Processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Should risk assessment processes be required to take into account additional or different criteria or risks than those listed in the proposed rule? If so, what additional factors should the Agencies consider requiring?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invites comment on specific factors or criteria banks should include in their risk assessment processes beyond those enumerated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for Incorporating Risk Assessment Results into AML/CFT Program
rubrics_metrics.description: How long does it generally take a bank to incorporate the results of a risk assessment into its AML/CFT program? What factors determine this time frame?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asks for practical information and factors affecting the time between assessment findings and program changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporating AML/CFT Priorities into Risk Assessment Processes
rubrics_metrics.description: What, if any, difficulties do banks anticipate when incorporating the AML/CFT Priorities as part of their risk assessment processes? What additional guidance on how to incorporate the AML/CFT Priorities into a bank's risk assessment processes would it be useful for the Agencies to provide?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seeks input on challenges and helpful guidance for operationalizing statutory AML/CFT Priorities within risk assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to Update Risk Assessment Processes Promptly Upon Significant Change
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule requires that risk assessment processes are updated promptly upon any change that the bank knows or has reason to know significantly changes the bank's money laundering, terrorist financing, and other illicit finance activity risks. Would the proposed update requirement change the way banks currently update their risk assessment processes, and if so how?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicits comment on need for clarification of 'promptly,' alternatives such as periodic updates, schedules, or using 'materially changes' instead of 'significantly changes.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback Loop Between ML/TF Risks and Risk Assessment Processes
rubrics_metrics.description: How do a bank's ML/TF risks and its risk assessment processes affect one another? If there is a feedback loop between the two, please describe it, including the typical amount of time between discovering new risks and incorporating those findings into risk assessment processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests empirical descriptions of the iterative relationship between observed risks and methodological updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent AML/CFT Program Testing (Internal or External)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the proposed rule, a bank is required to conduct independent AML/CFT program testing. Are further clarifications on the independent AML/CFT program testing requirement necessary to ensure that audits carried out by bank personnel or outside third parties are well-tailored, risk-based, and focused on effectiveness?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes this requirement aligns with existing independent audit function expectations and asks for comment on how institutions may interpret and carry out testing obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: AML/CFT Officer Location and Roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the proposed rule, while the AML/CFT officer must be located in the United States, personnel located outside of the United States would still be permitted to perform certain AML/CFT functions. This language does not alter existing regulations and guidance that generally prohibit the sharing of SARs with personnel located outside of the United States other than limited circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seeks comment on whether further clarifications are needed about permissible offshore functions and SAR-sharing limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written AML/CFT Program — Required Components, Form, and Level of Detail
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule standardizes the long-standing requirement that an AML/CFT program be written. Should the Agencies further clarify which specific elements of an institution's AML/CFT program must be written, or is this requirement generally understood in its current form?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asks in particular which components should be required in writing (e.g., risk assessment processes; internal policies, procedures, and controls; transaction monitoring rules; escalation and reporting protocols; independent testing results; training materials; documentation of designated personnel), what form such documentation should take (narrative, checklists, system configs, electronic records), and what level of detail is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval of Written AML/CFT Program by Board or Equivalent/Senior Management
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would require that a bank's written AML/CFT program be approved by its board of directors, an equivalent governing body within the bank, or appropriate senior management. Should the Agencies further clarify which aspects of the AML/CFT program must be subject to such approval?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions include whether approval is needed for each core component (risk assessment framework, policies, monitoring, testing, training, personnel designation), whether material revisions require re-approval, and what level of specificity the approving body should review (high-level architecture vs detailed procedures). Also asks whether alternatives to board approval would be appropriate and the benefits/drawbacks of eliminating a specified approval requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification for Supervision: What Constitutes a Significant or Systemic Failure
rubrics_metrics.description: Is clarification needed for banks to determine what constitutes a “significant or systemic failure” to implement an established AML/CFT program (in the supervision and enforcement context)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asks for input specifically relevant to supervisory thresholds and consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification for Supervision: What Constitutes Failure to Establish
rubrics_metrics.description: Is clarification needed for banks to determine what constitutes a “failure to establish an AML/CFT program” (in the supervision and enforcement context)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seeks supervisory-oriented examples and definitions to differentiate establishment failures from implementation failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: FinCEN Consultation Requirement Prior to Significant Supervisory Action
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would add a requirement for an agency to notify and consider information provided by FinCEN before initiating a significant AML/CFT supervisory action when acting pursuant to authority delegated under this chapter. Should the proposed consultation process include an asset threshold (e.g., consultation is required for any significant AML/CFT supervisory actions involving banks with $10 billion or more in assets)? Should the proposed rule provide the option for banks to request their agency consult with FinCEN prior to initiating a significant AML/CFT supervisory action?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seeks views on whether to limit consultation by asset threshold and whether to make consultation optional at a bank's request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of “Any Written Communication” in Definition of Significant Supervisory Action
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition of significant AML/CFT supervisory action includes the term “any written communication.” Is the term “any written communication” too broad? Are there downsides and negative consequences to including the term in the proposed regulatory text? Should it be more clearly defined or removed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests comment on breadth and potential unintended consequences of including a wide definition of written communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamlining FinCEN–Agency Consultation to Reduce Burden and Delays
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agencies recognize this adds additional layers of review for banks and the Agencies during an examination. Are there any avenues, communication channels, or methods in which FinCEN and the Agencies can streamline the consultation process and prevent logistical burdens for banks or delays in exam report issuance?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicits practical proposals to make the consultation process efficient while preserving intended oversight benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of “Significant AML/CFT Supervisory Action” and Inclusion of Unsafe or Unsound Practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the definition of the term “significant AML/CFT supervisory action” sufficiently clear? Does the inclusion of “unsafe or unsound practices or conditions” introduce confusion about what types of supervisory actions would be subject to the FinCEN consultation requirement, since those terms are not found in the BSA?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seeks comment on potential ambiguity introduced by bringing in supervisory terminology not in the BSA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of Confidential Supervisory Information to FinCEN and Privilege Concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Would the disclosure of confidential supervisory information to FinCEN compromise attorney-client privilege, other applicable privileges, or otherwise undermine the preservation of privilege in 12 U.S.C. 1821(t)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invites comment on legal privilege implications and safeguards if supervisory information is shared with FinCEN.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailoring Program Requirements or Implementation Timelines to Bank Size/Complexity/Risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Should the rule be revised to tailor program requirements or implementation timelines to the size, complexity, or risk profile of the bank?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asks whether formal tailoring by size or business model is appropriate, or whether the risk-based, scalable design of the proposal suffices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed Effective Date (12 Months) and Adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agencies are proposing an effective date of 12 months from the date of issuance of the final rule to allow sufficient time for financial institutions to review and implement their requirements. The Agencies solicit comment on the proposed effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests views on whether 12 months is sufficient and the tradeoffs of longer or shorter transition periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit Assessment: Reduction in Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule may improve AML/CFT program effectiveness, enabling banks to reallocate AML/CFT resources toward higher-risk customers and activities, which could reduce the frequency and severity of harm caused by criminal activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies discuss qualitative and quantitative challenges in measuring crime reduction benefits and invite comments on additional significant benefits to consider.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit Assessment: Increased Access to Financial Services for Low-Risk Clients
rubrics_metrics.description: An additional benefit of recalibrating AML/CFT programs toward higher-risk activities is that fewer low-risk clients would be denied access to banking services because of incorrect flags, potentially increasing financial access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies note lack of data to quantify this and invite commenters to provide input on scale and mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit Assessment: Increased Clarity, Supervisory Coherence, and Program Effectiveness for Banks
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule is expected to provide additional qualitative benefits from increased clarity and supervisory coherence, reducing regulatory fragmentation and promoting consistent supervisory outcomes across Agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies describe downstream benefits including reduced enforcement risk and better focus on higher-priority illicit activity; commenters may provide evidence or contrary views.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-Time Adjustment Costs to Banks
rubrics_metrics.description: If adopted, the proposed rule would require alignment of existing AML/CFT programs to the clarified requirements. Possible one-time costs include labor to update documentation, labor costs associated with ensuring the designated AML/CFT officer is located in the U.S. and has sufficient authority, and training costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies expect these costs to be minimal; they solicit data or alternative estimates from commenters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing Compliance Costs Assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agencies lack data to estimate how compliance costs would change under the proposed rule; however, factors suggest ongoing compliance costs would be similar to the baseline since requirements clarify rather than increase obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests comment and data on likely persistent changes in compliance costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternatives Considered — Prescriptive vs Flexible Risk-Based Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agencies considered more prescriptive program requirements (mandatory risk-assessment methodologies, specific governance structures, required technologies, defined timelines) but viewed such an approach as conflicting with the AML Act's emphasis on risk-based, flexible, outcome-oriented programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies rejected prescriptive approaches in favor of a flexible framework and invite comments on alternative approaches and their tradeoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) Analysis for Small Entities
rubrics_metrics.description: The agencies provide RFA analyses and certifications that the proposed rule would not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities, using thresholds (e.g., >5% of annual salaries and benefits or >2.5% of non-interest expenses) and agency-specific definitions of small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invites comments on the RFA analysis, whether thresholds and assumptions are appropriate, and whether the certification is justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) Information Collection Burden Estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: The NCUA proposes to extend with revision its information collection (OMB Control Number 3133-0108) and provides estimated annual burden hours (e.g., implementation: 32 hours per respondent .3 responses; ongoing: 8 hours per respondent annually), totaling 80,856 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NCUA invites comment on necessity, accuracy of burden estimates, ways to enhance clarity/utility of information collections, and ways to minimize burden (automation, tech).
